verified_signals.implies: The ATM fleet is essentially flat (+3 q/q) while merchant acquiring expands fast - spend will go to refresh/recycler conversion rather than fleet growth, plus POS hardware and managed services.
verified_signals.likelihood: High that the ATM fleet stays c.950-960 through 2026
verified_signals.followup: Track the same table in OTP's 2Q 2026 report (due Aug-2026); establish whether the POS jump is organic acquiring or a portfolio transfer.

verified_signals.signal: DSK's own live branch/ATM locator feed (dskbank.bg/GetOfficesData, independently re-pulled 31/07/2026) returns 817 locations: 726 carry an ATM (441 ATM-only sites, 285 branch+ATM) and 376 carry a branch (285 branch+ATM, 91 branch-only). 212 locations carry the 'Cash deposit' flag. CRITICAL STRUCTURE: 205 of those 212 are branch+ATM sites and only 7 are standalone ATM sites - so 72% of branch+ATM sites are deposit-capable, but only 7 of 441 off-branch ATM sites (1.6%) are. 192 locations have a 24h banking zone, 127 are open 24 hours, 3 are flagged 'Cashless office' and 1 has a kiosk device. CAVEAT: the flags are curated marketing labels, not a device inventory - only 167 locations carry an 'ATM for withdrawal' flag although 726 have ATMs - so treat 212 as a floor and the dispense-only count as approximate.
verified_signals.source_name: DSK Bank branch/ATM locator data feed (dskbank.bg/GetOfficesData?cultureName=en), linked from the Branch network page
verified_signals.implies: The recycler/CDM white space is overwhelmingly the OFF-BRANCH estate: 434 of 441 standalone ATM sites are dispense-only. In-branch cash-in is largely solved; off-branch cash-in is virtually greenfield. Only 3 cashless offices means the in-branch teller-cash-recycler (TCR) opportunity - a machine behind the counter that both accepts and re-dispenses notes to the teller - is essentially untouched.
verified_signals.likelihood: Medium-High that DSK expands deposit-capable ATMs during 2026-27 as euro cash habits settle
verified_signals.followup: Re-pull the feed quarterly to trend the 'Cash deposit' count; ask DSK cash management what deposit-ATM penetration they target OFF-branch specifically, since that is where the gap sits.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Independently re-pulled the feed with a desktop User-Agent (HTTP 200, 353KB) and recomputed every count in Python rather than trusting the researcher: 817 locations, 285 ATM+Branch, 441 ATM-only, 91 branch-only, 212 'Cash deposit', 192 '24h banking zone', 127 'Open 24 hours', 3 'Cashless office'. Every figure the researcher reported reproduces exactly. TWO MATERIAL ADDITIONS FROM MY OWN CROSS-TABS, which the researcher did not run: (1) I checked whether 'Cash deposit' contaminates branch-only sites (i.e. whether it means over-the-counter deposit rather than ATM deposit) - it does not, zero branch-only sites carry it, so the 212 are genuinely ATM locations and the researcher's denominator is sound; (2) but the flag is 205/7 split between branch+ATM and standalone ATM sites, which completely changes the sales story from the researcher's flat 'seven in ten ATM sites are dispense-only'. I also found the flags are inconsistently populated (167 'ATM for withdrawal' vs 726 ATM sites; 119 sites have Cash deposit but no withdrawal flag), so I added an explicit reliability caveat. Note 726 SITES vs 958 MACHINES from OTP's table - about 1.32 machines per site; the researcher was consistent in saying locations, but the two signals must not be mixed. opp_size XL retained: footprint-wide across 434 unconverted off-branch sites.

verified_signals.signal: DSK's FY2025 audited statements (in thousands of BGN) show 2025 additions to intangibles of BGN 34,664k separate / BGN 36,720k consolidated, of which BGN 34,591k (99.8% of the separate figure) sits in 'assets in the process of acquisition' - i.e. software still in build, not yet in service. Separate additions to property, plant and equipment were BGN 39,355k, but only BGN 2,104k went directly to IT equipment; a further BGN 36,673k was transferred INTO IT equipment from assets under construction, so BGN 38,777k was capitalised into IT equipment during 2025. IT-equipment net book value rose from BGN 40,566k to BGN 63,211k (+55.8%). Genuinely technology-directed 2025 capex is therefore c.BGN 73.4m (c.EUR 37.5m at the fixed rate of 1.95583).
verified_signals.source_name: DSK Bank AD Separate and Consolidated Financial Statements 2025, Note 33 (Property, plant and equipment) and Note 34 (Intangible assets)
verified_signals.implies: The 56% jump in IT-equipment NBV, driven by a large release of assets under construction into service, is consistent with a hardware refresh wave around the euro changeover - a live, sizeable budget line for self-service hardware, security and managed services. The large software work-in-progress balance also signals a build programme still running into 2026.
verified_signals.likelihood: High that elevated hardware capex continues into 2026
verified_signals.followup: Compare against the 1H-2026 statements when published; ask what share of IT-equipment additions was self-service hardware.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Downloaded the 4.9MB PDF and extracted it with pdfminer. My first grep for the researcher's figures returned NOTHING, which looked like fabrication - but the PDF uses non-breaking spaces as thousand separators ('39 355'), and on re-checking every single figure is present and exact: separate intangible additions 34,664; consolidated intangible additions 36,720; separate PPE additions 39,355; IT-equipment NBV 40,566 -> 63,211 (+55.83%). Reporting currency confirmed as thousands of BGN. CORRECTION TO THE FRAMING, not the figures: the researcher labelled BGN 74m (34,664 + 39,355) as 'combined technology/hardware capex'. That is wrong in composition - the 39,355 PPE figure covers ALL property, plant and equipment, and only 2,104 of it went to IT equipment directly (land and buildings 3, office equipment 6, other/under-construction 37,242). I traced the transfer line instead: 36,673 was transferred into IT equipment from assets under construction, giving 38,777 genuinely capitalised into IT equipment. Combined with intangibles that is c.BGN 73.4m / EUR 37.5m - very close to the researcher's number but arrived at correctly, and I have rewritten the signal to show the derivation. I also verified the researcher's network sentence ('5 regional centres, 51 financial centres, 23 business centres/zones, 85 branches, 109 bank offices') - it is on line 960 of the FY2025 report and the report itself dates it 'As of the end of 31 December 2024'. The researcher dated it correctly and honestly; it is DSK's own stale line inside a FY2025 document. It sums to 273, consistent with OTP's 273 branches at 31/03/2026. I removed it from the signal text because it is a 2024 backstory figure superseded by signal 1, and leaving it in a capex signal invites it being quoted as current.

verified_signals.signal: DSK disclosed a personal-data breach on 09/06/2026: the breach was detected in April 2026 and involved mishandled paper archives from the 2006-2018 period at its Lukovit office, directly affecting 475 individuals, caused by non-compliance with the bank's own archiving and document-destruction procedures. No IT systems were compromised. The Commission for Personal Data Protection (KZLD, Bulgaria's data-protection regulator) was notified and DSK says it is actively assisting the supervisory authority's ongoing actions; DSK opened a GDPR Article 34 lookup portal for affected clients.
verified_signals.source_name: DSK Bank notice: 'Информация за клиенти на Банка ДСК във връзка с нарушение на сигурността на лични данни'
verified_signals.implies: An open regulator process raises board attention on records management and data-security controls - an opening for secure document/records digitisation and for security and compliance managed services. Note the failure was procedural and paper-based, so the remedy is records handling and digitisation, not IT security hardening.
verified_signals.likelihood: Medium that remediation spend follows the KZLD outcome
verified_signals.followup: Track the KZLD decision and any fine or corrective order.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Fetched DSK's notice (HTTP 200) and read the full Bulgarian text. Confirmed exactly: 475 individuals ('Пряко засегнати са 475 физически лица'), Lukovit office, 2006-2018 servicing period, paper documents, cause stated as 'неспазване на установените правила и процедури за архивиране и унищожаване на документи на хартиен носител', KZLD notified, explicit statement that no DSK information systems were breached, and a lookup platform at dskbank.bg/справка-по-ззлд. ADDED one detail the researcher omitted that matters for timing: the breach was DETECTED in April 2026 and disclosed on 09/06/2026 - a roughly two-month gap that is itself relevant to how the regulator may view it. Also specified the Article 34 GDPR basis for the portal and spelled out what KZLD is. I sharpened the implies to note the failure was paper/procedural, because the researcher's 'data-security controls' phrasing could mislead into pitching IT security against a records-management failure. opp_size S and win Low retained - no remediation budget is disclosed and none should be assumed.

verified_signals.signal: BNB payment statistics show Bulgaria had 5,031 ATM terminals at end-H2 2025, down from 5,087 at end-2024 and 5,128 at end-H2 2023, while POS terminals jumped to 210,861 from 163,190. In H2 2025 there were 60.7m ATM cash withdrawals worth EUR 13.7bn against only 5.8m ATM cash deposits worth EUR 3.7bn - ATM deposit transactions are 9.6% of ATM withdrawal transactions. DECISIVE ADDITION: over-the-counter cash deposits at payment service providers in the same half were 9.7m transactions worth EUR 16.4bn - so branch-counter deposits still exceed ATM deposits by 1.7x in volume and 4.4x in value, and that counter volume is the migration headroom.
verified_signals.source_name: Bulgarian National Bank - Main indicators from the payment statistics for Bulgaria, semi-annual, EUR series (ps_mainindicators_new_eur_bg.xlsx), file last updated 22/07/2026
verified_signals.implies: A slowly shrinking national ATM base with a very low deposit share confirms the market-wide cash-in/recycler gap; DSK is roughly 19% of the national fleet. The EUR 16.4bn still crossing branch counters is the concrete, quantified prize for teller cash recyclers and deposit ATMs, and recyclers cut cash-in-transit cost per site, which is the commercial argument in a shrinking-fleet market.
verified_signals.likelihood: High that the national fleet keeps shrinking while deposit functionality grows
verified_signals.followup: Re-pull once BNB publishes H1-2026, the first post-euro half, to measure the euro effect on ATM deposits and on the counter-deposit volume.

verified_signals.signal: DSK became the largest bank in Bulgaria by assets in 1Q 2026 with c.EUR 23.5bn, displacing UBB (Обединена българска банка), which held EUR 22.75bn against DSK's EUR 22bn in 4Q 2025; UBB stood at EUR 20.6bn in 1Q 2026. DSK also reported a record month for consumer lending in March 2026 - new consumer loans +31% y/y, the highest monthly volume in DSK's history and, DSK says, in OTP Group's history - with average consumer-loan size +15% y/y. OTP reported DSK Group 1Q 2026 profit after tax of HUF 43.8bn (HUF 51.0bn adjusting for the full-year deposit-insurance fee booked in 1Q) and 19% ROE. On euro-area entry the mandatory reserve ratio fell from 12% to 1%, cutting DSK's required reserves from nearly EUR 2bn to about EUR 0.2bn - roughly EUR 1.8bn of liquidity released, which BNB paid no interest on.
verified_signals.source_name: OTP Bank Plc. Summary of the first quarter 2026 results (primary, for profit/ROE/reserves); dbr.bg banking-sector ranking (08/05/2026) and Bulgarian press for the asset ranking and consumer-lending record
verified_signals.implies: Market leadership plus a large, precisely quantified liquidity release means the balance sheet can fund a technology and self-service refresh without capital strain. The EUR 1.8bn freed from non-interest-bearing reserves is the concrete reason 2026 capex capacity is unusually good.
verified_signals.followup: Confirm against BNB banking-supervision statistics for 30/06/2026 when published; re-source the EUR 119.5bn sector-assets figure, which I could not verify.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Capital.bg (the researcher's cited source) returned HTTP 403, so I verified each component separately. From the OTP 1Q 2026 PDF I extracted directly: 'DSK Group generated HUF 43.8 billion profit after tax', 'implying a ROE of 19%', and 'the mandatory reserve ratio declined from 12% to 1%; as a result, required reserve amount decreased from the previous nearly EUR 2 billion to approximately EUR 0.2 billion from 2026' - all confirmed, and I have ADDED the EUR 2bn -> EUR 0.2bn detail because 'a large liquidity release' was vague where the primary source gives a hard number. The asset ranking is confirmed via dbr.bg (08/05/2026): DSK EUR 23.5bn, UBB EUR 20.6bn, and the 4Q 2025 reversal (UBB 22.75 vs DSK 22.0) - so the researcher's EUR 23.49bn and 'displacing UBB' are both right. The March 2026 consumer-lending record is confirmed via Bulgarian press: +31% y/y, highest monthly volume, average size +15% y/y, and I added the further detail that DSK claims it is also OTP Group's highest ever. ONE FIGURE I COULD NOT CONFIRM AND HAVE REMOVED: 'sector assets rose c.EUR 3bn in the quarter to EUR 119.5bn'. dbr.bg reports the top five banks at EUR 91.2bn representing 77.7% of the system, which implies roughly EUR 117.4bn - about EUR 2bn below the researcher's figure. Rather than publish either number I dropped the sector total and flagged it for re-sourcing against BNB supervision data. Source tier set to primary on the strength of the OTP report, with the press-sourced components attributed in source_name.

verified_signals.signal: On 20/07/2026 (published 21/07/2026) OTP Bank signed an agreement with a consortium of private equity funds managed by Blackstone, and DNB Bank, to acquire Luminor, the third-largest banking group in the Baltic region (Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania). Luminor's 2025 net profit was EUR 158m at 8.6% ROE, with a CET1 ratio of 20.2% at 31/12/2025. OTP states the deal increases group total assets by approximately 13% and takes OTP from 11 to 14 countries, with the euro-area share of the GROUP'S NET LOANS rising from 42% to 50%. Press reports Luminor's total assets at EUR 15.9bn and describe this as OTP's largest acquisition to date. Completion is subject to regulatory approvals; OTP gives no expected completion date.
verified_signals.source_name: OTP Group press release: 'OTP Bank to acquire Luminor, opening a new chapter in Baltic financial markets'
verified_signals.implies: A large integration will absorb group IT and change capacity into 2027-28, which can slow discretionary subsidiary programmes - but it also opens a new 3-country footprint where group-standard self-service and cash-automation vendors get re-decided. With no announced completion date, the timing of any effect on DSK is genuinely uncertain.
verified_signals.likelihood: Medium that DSK's discretionary IT roadmap is affected; High that group vendor standards get revisited
verified_signals.followup: Watch for the closing date and any group-level vendor consolidation announcements; OTP has published no completion timeline.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Fetched OTP's own release and read it in full. Confirmed: signed 20/07/2026 in Budapest and Tallinn, published 21/07/2026; Blackstone-managed private equity funds plus DNB Bank as sellers; Luminor described as 'the third-largest banking group in the Baltic region'; 2025 net profit EUR 158m at 8.6% ROE (I also added the CET1 of 20.2%); 14 countries, up from 11; 'Completion of the transaction is subject to obtaining the necessary regulatory approvals' with no timeline given. TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) The researcher wrote group assets lift 'by more than 10%'; that is the headline wording, but the body states 'approximately 13%' - corrected to the more precise figure. (2) The researcher wrote 'roughly half of operations inside the euro area'. The release is specific: it is the euro-zone share of the GROUP'S NET LOANS rising from 42% to 50%, not operations generally - corrected, because the loose version overstates the scope. TWO CLAIMS NOT IN THE PRIMARY SOURCE: Luminor's EUR 15.9bn total assets and 'OTP's largest deal to date' appear nowhere in OTP's release. Both are corroborated by wire-service-derived press (Investing.com, Stockopedia), so I kept them but attributed them explicitly to press rather than letting them read as OTP disclosures. I also added to the implies that the absence of any completion date makes the timing of knock-on effects on DSK genuinely uncertain, which the researcher asserted more confidently than the evidence supports.

residual_gaps: 1) ATM FLEET OEM AT DSK REMAINS UNIDENTIFIED - this is the single most valuable unanswered question in the unit and I independently re-tested it rather than accepting the researcher's conclusion. Bulgarian and English searches pairing DSK with NCR/NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, Wincor Nixdorf, and with procurement/maintenance terms, plus a check for any public Printec-DSK reference, returned nothing. The researcher's exhaustive-search conclusion stands. The only hardware fingerprint in any public document is DSK's own '40 to 150 notes per transaction depending on the ATM model', which establishes at least two acceptor generations but names no vendor. The operator route (field-team check or fascia photograph at one 150-note and one 40-note site) remains the practical answer. 2) VISA RELEASE WITHDRAWN - DSK's own page for the 26/03/2025 Visa exclusive-issuer release now 404s on both the raw and percent-encoded Cyrillic URL; that signal is press-sourced only and its confidence is Low as a result. The researcher recorded this URL as primary without noting it was dead. The '2.0m+ active cards' figure in the original signal could not be stood up in any source and was removed. 3) SECTOR ASSETS FIGURE UNVERIFIED - the 'EUR 119.5bn banking-sector assets, +c.EUR 3bn q/q' claim came from a Capital.bg article that returns HTTP 403. An independent source (dbr.bg) implies roughly EUR 117.4bn from the top-five share, about EUR 2bn lower, so I removed the figure pending a check against BNB banking-supervision statistics. 4) BLOCKED SOURCES LOGGED: capital.bg 403 (worked around via DSK's own media-centre copy of the Slaveykov interview, which upgraded that signal to primary); banker.bg 403; business.dir.bg 403; 3e-news behind a Cloudflare interstitial; dnevnik.bg 403 (Euromoney award). 5) EUROMONEY AWARD SCOPE - Euromoney's own Awards for Excellence 2026 Bulgaria page names UniCredit Bulbank as Bulgaria's Best Bank; DSK's retail-banking award is a separate category evidenced only in Bulgarian press, so it was removed from the AI signal rather than carried at primary strength. 6) LOCATOR FEED IS NOT A DEVICE INVENTORY - the 'Cash deposit' count of 212 is reliable as a floor, but the feature flags are inconsistently curated (only 167 of 726 ATM sites carry an 'ATM for withdrawal' flag), and 726 SITES do not map one-to-one to OTP's 958 MACHINES. Any device-level sizing needs confirmation from DSK directly. 7) OTP Integrated Annual Report 2025 (16MB) still not text-extracted; nothing in this file depends on it, but it remains the best untried route to a named self-service vendor.
